title_en: The Volcano That Gave Us Frankenstein
title_zh: 一座火山，造出了《弗兰肯斯坦》
english_paragraphs: In June 1816 a ceaseless downpour kept a party besieged at the Villa Diodati, a mansion the poet Lord Byron had leased on the outskirts of Geneva. After reading an anthology of German ghost stories in French translation, Byron proposed that each guest write a supernatural tale.

The melancholy weather was attributable to a distant blast. On 10 April 1815 Mount Tambora, on the Indonesian island of Sumbawa, blew itself apart in one of the most potent eruptions in recorded history. About 10,000 people died immediately, and tens of thousands more of starvation and disease in the aftermath.

The volcano pumped prodigious quantities of sulphur dioxide from its crater into the stratosphere, where it formed sulphate aerosols that blanketed the globe, reflecting sunshine and thereby lowering temperatures world-wide. Europe and North America came to know 1816 as the Year Without a Summer.
Europe's summer was chilly and relentlessly wet. Crops failed or lay rotten in saturated fields, cereal and bread prices escalated, and scarcity, disease, and unrest followed.

The eighteen-year-old Mary Godwin, later Mary Shelley, had set out in May alongside Percy Bysshe Shelley and Claire Clairmont. In her 1831 preface she would recollect a damp, gloomy summer whose torrents often kept the group indoors for days.

Byron's challenge proved fruitful. His physician John Polidori produced The Vampyre, whilst Byron's poetic output included Darkness. Mary began the ghastly yarn that became Frankenstein, which appeared anonymously in 1818 and was later reissued under her name. It is often called the founding work of the science-fiction genre.
A tropical volcano had supplied the rain, and a teenager the monster.

这种**阴郁**(melancholy)的天气，**归因于**(attributable to)一次远方的爆炸。1815年4月10日，坦博拉火山，位于**印度尼西亚的**(Indonesian)松巴哇岛上，**炸**(blew apart)**裂开来**(blew apart)，那是最**猛烈**(potent)的**喷发**(eruptions)之一，在有记录的历史上。约1万人当场死亡，而又有**数万**(tens of thousands)人死于**饥饿**(starvation)和疾病，发生在随后的**余波**(aftermath)中。

这座**火山**(volcano)**泵入了**(pumped)**庞大**(prodigious)数量的**二氧化硫**(sulphur dioxide)，从它的**火山口**(crater)送进平流层，在那里，它们形成了硫酸盐**气溶胶**(aerosols)，像毯子一样**笼罩了**(blanketed)全球，反射**阳光**(sunshine)，**从而**(thereby)**降低了**(lowering)**全世界**(world-wide)的气温。欧洲和北美后来**把**(know as)1816年**称作**(know as)无夏之年。

欧洲的夏天**寒冷**(chilly)，雨也**持续不断**(relentlessly)。**庄稼**(Crops failed)要么**歉收**(Crops failed)，要么**腐烂**(rotten)在**浸透了水的**(saturated)田地里，**谷物**(cereal)和面包价格**飞涨**(escalated)，（物资）**短缺**(scarcity)、疾病和**动荡**(unrest)随之而来。

**十八岁的**(eighteen-year-old)玛丽·戈德温，也就是后来的玛丽·雪莱，5月间就已**启程**(set out)，**结伴**(alongside)同行的有珀西·比希·雪莱和克莱尔·克莱蒙特。在她1831年的（书的）**序言**(preface)里，她**回忆**(recollect)说，那是一个**潮湿**(damp)、**阴沉的**(gloomy)夏天，那个夏天的**倾盆大雨**(torrents)常常把大家困在屋里好几天。

拜伦的挑战结果**成果丰硕**(fruitful)。他的医生约翰·波利多里写出了《吸血鬼》，**与此同时**(whilst)，拜伦**诗歌的**(poetic)**产出**(output)中有《黑暗》。玛丽开始写那个**恐怖**(ghastly)的**故事**(yarn)，它后来成了**《弗兰肯斯坦》**(Frankenstein)，这部作品1818年**匿名**(anonymously)出版，后来又以她的名字**重新发行**(reissued)。这部作品常被称为**科幻**(science-fiction)**体裁/类型**(genre)的**开山之作**(founding work)。
一座**热带的火山**(tropical volcano)提供了大雨，然而一位少女却创造了**怪物**(monster)。

sentences.english: About 10,000 people died immediately, and tens of thousands more of starvation and disease in the aftermath.
sentences.chinese_source: 约1万人当场死亡，而又有**数万**(tens of thousands)人死于**饥饿**(starvation)和疾病，发生在随后的**余波**(aftermath)中。

sentences.english: The volcano pumped prodigious quantities of sulphur dioxide from its crater into the stratosphere, where it formed sulphate aerosols that blanketed the globe, reflecting sunshine and thereby lowering temperatures world-wide.
sentences.chinese_source: 这座**火山**(volcano)**泵入了**(pumped)**庞大**(prodigious)数量的**二氧化硫**(sulphur dioxide)，从它的**火山口**(crater)送进平流层，在那里，它们形成了硫酸盐**气溶胶**(aerosols)，像毯子一样**笼罩了**(blanketed)全球，反射**阳光**(sunshine)，**从而**(thereby)**降低了**(lowering)**全世界**(world-wide)的气温。

sentences.english: Europe and North America came to know 1816 as the Year Without a Summer.
sentences.chinese_source: 欧洲和北美后来**把**(know as)1816年**称作**(know as)无夏之年。

sentences.english: Europe's summer was chilly and relentlessly wet.
sentences.chinese_source: 欧洲的夏天**寒冷**(chilly)，雨也**持续不断**(relentlessly)。

sentences.english: Crops failed or lay rotten in saturated fields, cereal and bread prices escalated, and scarcity, disease, and unrest followed.
sentences.chinese_source: **庄稼**(Crops failed)要么**歉收**(Crops failed)，要么**腐烂**(rotten)在**浸透了水的**(saturated)田地里，**谷物**(cereal)和面包价格**飞涨**(escalated)，（物资）**短缺**(scarcity)、疾病和**动荡**(unrest)随之而来。

sentences.english: The eighteen-year-old Mary Godwin, later Mary Shelley, had set out in May alongside Percy Bysshe Shelley and Claire Clairmont.
sentences.chinese_source: **十八岁的**(eighteen-year-old)玛丽·戈德温，也就是后来的玛丽·雪莱，5月间就已**启程**(set out)，**结伴**(alongside)同行的有珀西·比希·雪莱和克莱尔·克莱蒙特。

sentences.english: In her 1831 preface she would recollect a damp, gloomy summer whose torrents often kept the group indoors for days.
sentences.chinese_source: 在她1831年的（书的）**序言**(preface)里，她**回忆**(recollect)说，那是一个**潮湿**(damp)、**阴沉的**(gloomy)夏天，那个夏天的**倾盆大雨**(torrents)常常把大家困在屋里好几天。
拜伦的挑战结果**成果丰硕**(fruitful)。

sentences.english: His physician John Polidori produced The Vampyre, whilst Byron's poetic output included Darkness.
sentences.chinese_source: 他的医生约翰·波利多里写出了《吸血鬼》，**与此同时**(whilst)，拜伦**诗歌的**(poetic)**产出**(output)中有《黑暗》。

sentences.english: Mary began the ghastly yarn that became Frankenstein, which appeared anonymously in 1818 and was later reissued under her name.
sentences.chinese_source: 玛丽开始写那个**恐怖**(ghastly)的**故事**(yarn)，它后来成了**《弗兰肯斯坦》**(Frankenstein)，这部作品1818年**匿名**(anonymously)出版，后来又以她的名字**重新发行**(reissued)。

sentences.english: It is often called the founding work of the science-fiction genre.
sentences.chinese_source: 这部作品常被称为**科幻**(science-fiction)**体裁/类型**(genre)的**开山之作**(founding work)。

sentences.english: A tropical volcano had supplied the rain, and a teenager the monster.
sentences.chinese_source: 一座**热带的火山**(tropical volcano)提供了大雨，然而一位少女却创造了**怪物**(monster)。

approved_summary: 1815年，印尼坦博拉火山喷发，当场约一万人死亡，随后又有数万人死于饥饿和疾病。
火山喷出的二氧化硫在高空形成硫酸盐微粒，反射阳光降温，使1816年成为欧美无夏之年。
欧洲夏季寒冷多雨，庄稼歉收、粮价上涨，饥饿、疾病与社会动荡接踵而来。
大雨把拜伦、玛丽·雪莱等人困在日内瓦郊外的别墅，拜伦提议每人写一篇恐怖故事。
18岁的玛丽开始写《弗兰肯斯坦》，1818年匿名出版，这部作品后来常被视为科幻小说的开山之作。
